Max and Mia are taking a closer look at spring flowers and bees at the park.

They want to know more about the relationship between flowering plants and the animals that visit them.

Explore Max and Mia's questions:

1. Name the different parts of a flower
2. How do organisms help plants to reproduce? 
3. What are these processes called?

Share your ideas using the Documentation tool.

Use the bricks:

Build a model of a bee flying around a flower full of pollen.
<font size="3">Program your bee to stop at the flower to collect pollen.</font>

Turn on the Smarthub and connect it to your device. Watch the video if you need help.

Refer to the Help panel for more guidance.

Use your model:

Build another pollinator that would be attracted by a different flower.

Consider one of the following:
1. Tubular flowers are best suited to birds. 
2. Butterflies are attracted to flowers with certain colours. 
3. Pollination can happen between two different flowers. 

Document how your flower and pollinator are suited to each other.

Finalise your document:

1. Explain the limitations of your model.
2. Organise your information.
3. Insert important text, pictures, screenshots or videos to describe how your model represents an organism helping a plant to reproduce.

Share your findings:

Present in your own words, how pollinators can contribute to plant reproduction. Be sure to point out specific examples of how your model demonstrates this. Share at least one limitation of your model.

Use your model further 
with Max and Mia

How do certain organisms contribute to the life cycle of plants?

In this project, you will:
• Explore how different organisms take an active role in plant reproduction.
• Create and program a model of a bee and flower to represent the relationship between the pollinator and the plant.
• Present and document the different models you have created to depict plants and their pollinators.

Use your model further:

Build the plant after the flower has been pollinated and show how the seeds are dispersed:

Consider one of the following:
1. Seeds dispersed from flowering plants or non-flowering plants 
2. Seeds dispersed by organisms
3. Seeds dispersed in other ways

Document the seed dispersion process that you have chosen to model.
